actor.operator: Any operator within the meaning of Art 3(8) (provider, product manufacturer, deployer, authorised representative, importer or distributor).
actor.product_manufacturer: Manufacturer of a product covered by Annex I legislation.
actor.gpai_model_provider: Provider of a general-purpose AI model.
actor.notified_body: Conformity assessment body notified under the Act.

actor.ai_office: The AI Office (part of the Commission).

factVocabulary.firstPlacedOnMarketOrPutIntoServiceDate: date | unknown. Date on which the first unit of the system's type and model was lawfully placed on the Union market or put into service. Recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 makes this the decisive date for the Art 111(2) grace period. The Art 111(1) entry and the exceptIf lists that leave out the Art 111(1) systems use the same fact, although recital (39) states the rule only for Art 111(2); that reuse is an assumption (LR-03).
factVocabulary.placedOnMarketDate: date | unknown. Date on which the AI system was first placed on the Union market. Art 111(4) uses it; how a system that was only put into service is treated is LR-04.
factVocabulary.gpaiModelPlacedOnMarketDate: date | unknown. Date the general-purpose AI model was first placed on the Union market.
factVocabulary.generatesSyntheticContent: boolean | unknown. The AI system (including a general-purpose AI system) generates synthetic audio, image, video or text content.
factVocabulary.highRiskRoute: annex_iii | annex_i_section_a | annex_i_section_b | not_high_risk | unknown. Classification route under Art 6, derived from the reviewed classification route (annexRoute in Classification, site-app/lib/domain/classification.ts, re-exported from site-app/lib/domain.ts; mapping in RD-27).
factVocabulary.significantDesignChangeOnOrAfterChapterI: boolean | unknown. The system has been subject to significant changes in its design on or after the Chapter III application date for its route.
factVocabulary.intendedForUseByPublicAuthorities: boolean | unknown. The high-risk AI system is intended to be used by public authorities (Art 111(2), second sentence).
factVocabulary.annexXLargeScaleItComponent: boolean | unknown. Component of a large-scale IT system established by the legal acts listed in Annex X.

predicateOperators.in: fact is one of the listed values
predicateOperators.before: date fact is strictly earlier than value
predicateOperators.onOrAfter: date fact is on or after value

vocabularies.predicateRule: Predicates select candidate rules only. Each predicate list is a conjunction evaluated in three-valued logic: false if any predicate is false, true if all are true, otherwise unknown. An entry or transitional record is a candidate when appliesIf is true (an absent list counts as true) and exceptIf is false (an absent list counts as false). An unknown result yields needs_information, never a pass or a not-applicable decision. obligationsApplyOnlyIf states when the obligations reach a legacy system. Applicability remains a reviewed human decision.
vocabularies.crossReferenceRule: A transitional record with entryId restates the standalone applicationDates or authorityDeadlines entry it names and carries the same deadline and predicates. List the rule once, under that entry, and show the record as a cross-reference. In prohibitedPractices, entryId names the applicationDates entry that dates the point.

provisions: Art 5(1), first subparagraph, points (a), (b) and (c) to (h)
applicationDates.scope: Chapter II, except the points added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
applicationDates.summary: Prohibited AI practices: placing on the market, putting into service or use (point (h): use) of AI systems for the eight original practices. See prohibitedPractices.

legalBasis.amendedBy: Point (a) replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (40)(a); the 2 Feb 2025 date is unchanged for these points.

transitional.rule: The Art 111 carve-outs for legacy systems are expressly without prejudice to Art 5; Art 5 applies to legacy systems.

applicationDates.summary: AI literacy. As replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (in force 27 Jul 2026): providers and deployers must take measures to support the AI literacy of staff and others operating or using AI systems on their behalf, taking into account knowledge, experience, education, training and context. The duty does not require them to guarantee any specific level of literacy of any individual. The original text required measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy.

legalBasis.amendedBy: Art 4 replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (5); the replacement text is in force from 2026-07-27.

applicationDates.summary: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models: technical documentation (Annex XI), information for downstream providers (Annex XII), copyright policy, public summary of training content (Art 53); authorised representatives for providers established outside the Union (Art 54); additional obligations for models with systemic risk (Art 55).

transitional.rule: Providers of GPAI models placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025 must take the necessary steps to comply by 2 Aug 2027.

applicationDates.scope: Notifying authorities and notified bodies, governance, penalties (except Art 101) and confidentiality
applicationDates.summary: Rules on notifying authorities and notified bodies, EU and national governance, national penalty regimes and confidentiality apply. Art 101 (fines on GPAI model providers) is excepted and applies from 2 Aug 2026. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 added Art 28(8) and (9) (single application and unified assessment for Annex I Section A notified bodies) and Art 99(6a) (lower-of fine caps for SMCs), in force from 27 Jul 2026.

applicationDates.scope: Entry into force of the Digital Omnibus on AI; Arts 102 to 110 (amendments to other Union acts, including Directive (EU) 2020/1828)
applicationDates.summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 enters into force, so amended text in chapters that already applied (for example Art 3(14), (14a), (14b), Art 4 and the new Art 4a) takes effect from this date. Arts 102 to 110 of the AI Act apply from this date under the new point (d). This is the effective date of the consolidated version 02024R1689-20260727.

legalBasis.reference: Art 4 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; Art 113, third paragraph, point (d)
legalBasis.amendedBy: Point (d) added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (40)(c).

applicationDates.scope: Chapter I (inserted) and Chapter III Section 2 (Art 10 references)
applicationDates.summary: Legal basis for processing special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction, replacing Art 10(5). See specialCategoryData for the exact conditions.

legalBasis.reference: Art 113, third paragraph, point (a) (Chapter I) read with entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
legalBasis.amendedBy: Art 4a inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (6); Art 10 amended by Art 1, point (9).

applicationDates.notes: Recital (9) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 says the Art 4a legal basis should apply from the date of entry into application of 'that Regulation', so that providers can prepare for Art 10(2)(f) and (g) before the high-risk requirements apply. The Art 10 duties that Art 4a(1) serves apply from the Chapter III dates (2 Dec 2027 or 2 Aug 2028).

provisions: Every provision not covered by Art 113, third paragraph, points (a) to (d)
applicationDates.scope: Default date. Notably Chapter III Section 5 (Arts 40 to 49), Chapter IV (Art 50), Chapter VI (Arts 57 to 63, including new Art 60a), Chapter VIII (Art 71), Chapter IX (Arts 72 to 94, including new Arts 75a to 75d), Chapter X (Arts 95 and 96), Chapter XI (Arts 97 and 98), Art 101 and Art 6(5).
applicationDates.summary: General date of application of the AI Act. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 did not change it.

Providers: inform people they are interacting with an AI system (50(1)); mark outputs of systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text in a machine-readable format and make them detectable (50(2)). Deployers: inform people exposed to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation (50(3)); disclose deep fakes and AI-generated or manipulated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest (50(4)). Information must be given clearly at the latest at first interaction or exposure (50(5)). These duties sit alongside Chapter III duties (50(6)).
conditions: Each paragraph has its own exceptions (for example law-enforcement authorisation; assistive editing functions under 50(2); human review or editorial control for text under 50(4)).
Art 50(7) as replaced: the Commission assesses whether codes of practice are adequate for 50(2) and 50(4) and may adopt implementing acts if not.

legalBasis.amendedBy: Art 50(7) replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (20); Art 50(1) to (6) unchanged.

transitional.rule: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content that were placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 must take the necessary steps to comply with Art 50(2) by 2 Dec 2026. Only Art 50(2) is transitioned.

applicationDates.scope: Commission supervision and fines for providers of general-purpose AI models
applicationDates.summary: The Commission can enforce the Chapter V obligations against GPAI model providers, including fines under Art 101.

legalBasis.reference: Art 113, second paragraph, and the exception for Art 101 in point (b)

applicationDates.scope: Chapter IX Section 3, AI Office supervision of certain AI systems
applicationDates.summary: The AI Office is exclusively competent to supervise and enforce the Act for (a) AI systems based on a general-purpose AI model where model and system come from the same provider or undertaking, and (b) AI systems that constitute or are integrated into a designated very large online platform or search engine. Point (a) excludes Annex I products, Annex III point 2 systems, systems of law enforcement, border management and financial institutions within Art 74(6), and Annex III point 8 systems for the administration of justice. The competence applies to providers, and to deployers only where they are the provider or part of its undertaking. Providers of high-risk systems under AI Office competence report serious incidents to the AI Office (75(1a)). Arts 75a to 75d set the AI Office's powers, commitments, fines and periodic penalty payments, and safeguards.

legalBasis.amendedBy: Art 75 amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (31); Arts 75a to 75d inserted by Art 1, point (32).

applicationDates.scope: Provisions that apply on the general date on the text but attach to high-risk AI systems
applicationDates.summary: Standards, conformity assessment, declaration, CE marking, registration, the EU database, post-market monitoring and serious-incident reporting are not named in Art 113(c), so on the text they apply from 2 Aug 2026. The operator duties that trigger them (for example Art 16 and Art 6(4)) sit in Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 and apply only from 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) or 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I). Treat the operative date of each duty as a legal-review question; do not compute readiness from 2 Aug 2026 alone.

legalBasis.reference: Art 113, second paragraph, read with point (c)

applicationDates.scope: Chapter II, prohibitions added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
applicationDates.summary: Prohibited: placing on the market, putting into service or use of AI systems that (ba) generate or manipulate realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable person's intimate parts, or of an identifiable person engaged in sexually explicit activities, without that person's freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent; or (bb) generate or manipulate child sexual abuse material or performance within the meaning of Art 2(c) and (e) of Directive 2011/93/EU, except where a 'without right' defence applies under national law.
conditions: Art 5(1a)(a), providers: placing on the market or putting into service is prohibited only where (i) that generation or manipulation is the system's intended purpose, or (ii) the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make it a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification, and the system lacks reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards to reliably prevent it (taking into account reasonably foreseeable misuse) and to correct observed or reported misuse.
Art 5(1a)(b), deployers: use is prohibited only where the deployer uses the system for the purpose of generating or manipulating such material or performance.
Art 5(1b), point (ba) only: manipulation that does not increase the exposure of depicted intimate parts or alter the nature of depicted sexually explicit activities is not manipulation.

legalBasis.reference: Art 113, third paragraph, point (a), as replaced
legalBasis.amendedBy: Points (ba) and (bb) inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (7)(a); paragraphs 1a and 1b inserted by Art 1, point (7)(b); date set by Art 1, point (40)(a). Recitals (10) to (14) explain scope.

transitional.rule: No legacy carve-out: the Art 111 carve-outs are without prejudice to Art 5.

applicationDates.scope: End of the Art 50(2) marking transition for generative systems already on the market
applicationDates.summary: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content that were placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 must take the necessary steps to comply with Art 50(2) (machine-readable marking and detectability of outputs) by 2 Dec 2026. Systems placed on the market on or after 2 Aug 2026 have been subject to Art 50(2) since placing on the market.
conditions: Recital (38) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 describes this as a four-month transitional period.

legalBasis.amendedBy: Paragraph 4 added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (39)(b).

applicationDates.scope: General-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025
applicationDates.summary: Providers of GPAI models placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025 must take the necessary steps to comply with the Regulation's obligations by 2 Aug 2027.

provisions: Chapter III Section 1 (Arts 6 and 7, except Art 6(5))
applicationDates.scope: AI systems classified as high-risk under Art 6(2) and Annex III
applicationDates.summary: Classification rules, requirements (risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency to deployers, human oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity) and the obligations of providers, importers, distributors, value-chain actors and deployers apply to Annex III systems, including deployer duties (Art 26) and the fundamental rights impact assessment (Art 27).

legalBasis.reference: Art 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i), as replaced

transitional.rule: For high-risk systems, other than the Art 111(1) systems, placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (2 Dec 2027 for Annex III), the Regulation applies to their operators only if, as from that date, the systems are subject to significant changes in their designs. Recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the grace period attaches to the type and model, and the decisive date is when its first unit was placed on the market or put into service. Without prejudice to Art 5. The original text used the fixed date 2 Aug 2026.

In any case, providers and deployers of these legacy high-risk systems that are intended to be used by public authorities must take the necessary steps to comply by 2 Aug 2030, whether or not the design changes.

Components of the large-scale IT systems listed in Annex X placed on the market or put into service before 2 Aug 2027 must be brought into compliance by 31 Dec 2030. Art 111(2) covers high-risk systems other than these.

provisions: Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 (Arts 6 to 27, except Art 6(5))
applicationDates.scope: AI systems classified as high-risk under Art 6(1) and Annex I (safety components of, or themselves, products under Union harmonisation legislation that need third-party conformity assessment)
applicationDates.summary: Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply to Annex I high-risk systems. For products under Annex I Section B legislation, only Art 6(1), Art 60a and Arts 102 to 112 apply, and Arts 57 to 59 only in so far as the requirements have been integrated into that legislation (Art 2(2)). Annex I Section A point 1 (Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC) is deleted and Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery is added as Section B point 21. New Art 6(1a) to (1c) narrow what counts as a safety component and when the third-party assessment condition is met.

legalBasis.reference: Art 113, third paragraph, point (c)(ii), as replaced

transitional.rule: For high-risk systems, other than the Art 111(1) systems, placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (2 Aug 2028 for Annex I), the Regulation applies to their operators only if, as from that date, the systems are subject to significant changes in their designs. Recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: the grace period attaches to the type and model, and the decisive date is when its first unit was placed on the market or put into service. Without prejudice to Art 5. The original text used the fixed date 2 Aug 2026.

In any case, providers and deployers of these legacy high-risk systems that are intended to be used by public authorities must take the necessary steps to comply by 2 Aug 2030, whether or not the design changes.

Components of the large-scale IT systems listed in Annex X placed on the market or put into service before 2 Aug 2027 must be brought into compliance by 31 Dec 2030. Art 111(2) covers high-risk systems other than these.

For Art 6(1) systems, specific requirements in Arts 9 to 15 and 17 to 25 may be limited where Annex I Section A legislation gives equivalent or higher protection; the Commission must adopt delegated acts specifying this by 2 Aug 2027.
Notified bodies notified under Annex I Section A legislation must apply for designation under the AI Act by 28 Jan 2028.

applicationDates.scope: Annex III high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities whose type and model was first placed on the market or put into service before 2 Dec 2027 (the Annex III date of application of Chapter III), other than the Art 111(1) systems
applicationDates.summary: Providers and deployers of these legacy systems must take the necessary steps to comply with the Regulation's requirements and obligations by 2 Aug 2030, whether or not the systems undergo significant design changes. A significant design change from 2 Dec 2027 brings the obligations forward to the date of the change (first sentence). A system first placed on the market or put into service on or after 2 Dec 2027 is not a legacy system: the Regulation applies to it from that point, so this deadline does not concern it.

legalBasis.reference: Art 111(2), second sentence, read with Art 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i)
legalBasis.amendedBy: Paragraph 2 replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (39)(a): the cut-off is now the Chapter III date for the route; the 2 Aug 2030 date is unchanged.

applicationDates.notes: exceptIf leaves out the Art 111(1) systems (Annex X components placed on the market or put into service before 2 Aug 2027): Art 111(2) covers high-risk systems 'other than the systems referred to in paragraph 1', and recital (177) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 gives the two groups their deadlines 'respectively'. Whether the second sentence carries that exclusion is part of LR-03.

applicationDates.scope: Annex I high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities whose type and model was first placed on the market or put into service before 2 Aug 2028 (the Annex I date of application of Chapter III), other than the Art 111(1) systems
applicationDates.summary: Providers and deployers of these legacy systems must take the necessary steps to comply with the Regulation's requirements and obligations by 2 Aug 2030, whether or not the systems undergo significant design changes. A significant design change from 2 Aug 2028 brings the obligations forward to the date of the change (first sentence). A system first placed on the market or put into service on or after 2 Aug 2028 is not a legacy system: the Regulation applies to it from that point, so this deadline does not concern it.

specialCategoryData.provision: Art 4a, Processing of special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction
specialCategoryData.replaces: Art 10(5), deleted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (9)(b)

paragraph1.purpose: Bias detection and correction in accordance with Art 10(2)(f) and (g).
paragraph1.threshold: Exceptionally, to the extent strictly necessary, subject to appropriate safeguards for fundamental rights and freedoms, and in addition to Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 as applicable.

allConditionsRequired.condition: Bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data.
Technical limitations on re-use of the data, and state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation.
Measures to secure and protect the data, with suitable safeguards including strict controls and documentation of access, so that only authorised persons with confidentiality obligations have access.
The data are not transmitted, transferred or otherwise accessed by other parties.
The data are deleted once the bias has been corrected or the data have reached the end of their retention period, whichever comes first.

The records of processing activities under Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 include why the processing was strictly necessary to detect and correct biases and why other data could not achieve that objective.

paragraph2.who: Providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, and deployers of high-risk AI systems.

conditions.condition: The processing is strictly necessary for bias detection and correction in view of possible biases likely to affect health and safety, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where outputs influence inputs for future operations.
All conditions and safeguards of paragraph 1 are applied.

paragraph2.noObligation: Paragraph 2 does not create an obligation to conduct bias detection and correction.

presumptionOfConformity.statutoryBasis: Art 40(1), unchanged: systems in conformity with cited harmonised standards are presumed to conform with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2 (Arts 8 to 15) or, as applicable, the obligations of Chapter V Sections 2 and 3, to the extent the standards cover them. Art 17 is in Chapter III Section 3. Art 40(2), fourth subparagraph, added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (17): the Commission must request standardisation deliverables, including harmonised standards as appropriate, that facilitate joint compliance and presumption of conformity with the requirements or obligations of Chapter III Sections 2 and 3 and with the relevant requirements and obligations of the Annex I legislation (recital (21)). That subparagraph governs standardisation requests and does not amend Art 40(1). EN 18286 was requested earlier, under C(2025) 3871 of 23 June 2025. Recital (1) of Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 summarises Art 40 as a presumption for the requirements the standards cover, without the Section 2 limit.

legalReviewItems.question: Art 40(1), unchanged, grants a presumption for Chapter III Section 2 requirements (Arts 8 to 15) and Chapter V obligations; Art 17 sits in Section 3. The fourth subparagraph of Art 40(2), added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (17), requires the Commission to request deliverables that facilitate joint compliance and presumption of conformity with the requirements or obligations of Chapter III Sections 2 and 3 and the relevant Annex I legislation (recital (21)), but it does not amend Art 40(1), and EN 18286 was requested earlier under C(2025) 3871. Recital (1) of Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 summarises Art 40 without the Section 2 limit, and the Commission and CEN-CENELEC describe a presumption for the Art 17 requirements the standard covers. Secondary sources say Annex ZA maps Art 17(1) and the first sentence of Art 11(1). Confirm the legal basis and exact scope, and check Annex ZA in a licensed copy.

legalReviewItems.topic: Operative date of high-risk-linked provisions outside Chapter III Sections 1 to 3
legalReviewItems.question: Chapter III Section 5 (Arts 40 to 49), Art 71 and Arts 72 and 73 fall under the 2 Aug 2026 general date on the text, but the duties that trigger them (Art 16, Art 6(4), Art 26) apply from 2 Dec 2027 or 2 Aug 2028. Confirm the operative date per duty (registration, declaration, CE marking, post-market monitoring, serious-incident reporting).

Which 'date of application of Chapter III' is the cut-off (assumed: the point (c) date for the system's route, set by the first unit of the type and model under recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); whether the 2 Aug 2027 date in Art 111(1) is also set by the first unit of the type and model (recital (39) states that rule only for Art 111(2); the data assumes it is, in the 31 Dec 2030 entry and in the exceptIf lists that leave out the Art 111(1) systems); what counts as 'significant changes in their designs' (recital (177) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 treats it as equivalent in substance to a substantial modification); whether the 2 Aug 2030 sentence, like the first sentence, excludes the Art 111(1) systems (recital (177) gives the two groups their deadlines 'respectively'; the data assumes it does); and whether the carve-out ('this Regulation shall apply ... only if') also suspends duties outside Chapter III, such as Art 50, for legacy high-risk systems.

The transition covers systems 'placed on the market' before 2 Aug 2026. Confirm the treatment of systems only put into service (for example in-house) before that date, and whether new versions or new distribution channels after 2 Aug 2026 count as a new placing on the market.

How auditors should evidence 'reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification' and 'reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards' under Art 5(1a)(a)(ii), including for open-source releases and API access; and how the consent condition in point (ba) is evidenced.

Confirm that Art 4a applies from 27 Jul 2026 (recital (9) refers to the date of entry into application of 'that Regulation'), and whether an external auditor or audit platform is an 'other party' under Art 4a(1)(d), so that special-category data may not be transferred to it under Art 4a.

legalReviewItems.topic: Amended text in chapters that already applied
legalReviewItems.question: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 sets no separate application date for amendments to Chapters I and II other than the new Art 5 points. Confirm that the replaced Art 4, the amended Art 3 definitions and Art 4a take effect on 27 Jul 2026.
Confirm that the replaced Art 75(1) and Arts 75a to 75d operate from 2 Aug 2026 (Chapter IX general date) and how the exceptions in Art 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv) apply to the engagement's system.

The new safety-component clarifications sit in Chapter III Section 1 and so apply from the point (c) dates. Confirm whether classification work before those dates should already apply them (readiness).

legalReviewItems.topic: Annex I Section B and machinery
legalReviewItems.question: Confirm the consequences of moving Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 to Annex I Section B (point 21): under Art 2(2) only Art 6(1), Art 60a and Arts 102 to 112 apply, and Art 3 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amends the Machinery Regulation, whose related delegated acts apply by 2 Aug 2028. This also decides what the Art 111(2) legacy rule and the 2 Aug 2030 public-authority deadline require of Section B systems.
